title: Natural Guardians of a Hindu Minor — Section 6 HMGA

content.overview: Section 6 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 names the natural guardians of a Hindu minor in respect of the minor’s person and property (excluding undivided interest in joint family property). For a boy or an unmarried girl, the father, and after him the mother; for an illegitimate boy or illegitimate unmarried girl, the mother, and after her the father; for a married girl, the husband. The proviso qualifies the father’s priority where he has ceased to be a Hindu or has completely renounced the world.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Hindu minor? (2) Legitimate/illegitimate/married girl? (3) Father then mother (or reverse for illegitimate)? (4) Undivided joint-family interest excluded?
content.study:
Natural guardianship under s. 6 is statutory. The welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration under s. 13 whenever a court is called upon to appoint or declare a guardian.

Undivided interest in joint family property is excluded from the property covered by natural guardianship under this section.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Order for legitimate minors
sections.body: Boy or unmarried girl: father, and after him the mother.

sections.heading: Illegitimate minors
sections.body: Mother, and after her the father.

sections.heading: Proviso
sections.body: Father’s claim fails if he has ceased to be a Hindu or has completely and finally renounced the world.

sections.heading: Exclusion
sections.body: Undivided interest in joint family property is outside s. 6 property guardianship.

provisions.title: Natural guardians of a Hindu minor

examples.title: Father then mother
examples.body: Legitimate minor boy — father is natural guardian; after father, mother.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 6 decide every custody dispute alone?
hypotheticals.analysis: Natural guardianship is statutory under s. 6, but court decisions on appointment/declaration are controlled by the paramount welfare principle in s. 13.

distinctions.title: s. 6 natural guardians vs s. 13 welfare
distinctions.right: Welfare of the minor is paramount in court decisions.

misconceptions.trap: Father always prevails over mother regardless of welfare.
misconceptions.correction: s. 6 states the natural order; s. 13 makes welfare paramount when the court decides.
